body:
I need drafted dialogue for a scene at Ireena's window, two short Narrator lines, some road lines, and some epilogue text, all about Izek Strazni. Reply with the nodes below only, in the order given, no commentary.

# Part C

## Scene: Strahd at Ireena's window, with Izek guarding

Ireena shelters at the Blue Water Inn, or in a house behind Krezk's wall. At night the vampire lord Strahd (never named) comes to her window and stands on nothing outside it; she stands entranced at the open casement, going to him. Her brother Izek has been sitting guard at her door, and his scaled arm burns him awake when the vampire is near. In the existing scene the party arrives at the window, and if Ismark is guarding her instead he is deeply and unnaturally asleep by the door; the party must stop him (a holy symbol, a prayer, a plea, or by going for him). This is the way where Izek stops it. The vampire lord is courteous, patient and amused; he never threatens; he steps back from fire and from kin. Do not have him say anything about the night in the woods when Izek was nine.

Existing lines of the scene, so you hear it (do NOT repeat): "Ah. My guests. You are just in time to say goodbye." / "He's right. I'm so tired of running. It's only a window." / "Keep your trinket. It will not keep her." / "Not tonight, then. I can wait. I have had a great deal of practice."

~ window_izek_inn: Narrator x1 (in place of the sleeping Ismark: Izek is on his feet in the doorway of Ireena's room at the Blue Water Inn, awake, the scaled arm lit like a forge coal).
~ window_izek_krezk: Narrator x1 (the same in the house behind Krezk's wall: lit arm, upstairs room, the shutters hanging open).
~ izek_window: the party lets Izek take the window (the option row in the existing menu says: "Let Izek take the window."). Narrator x1 (he walks past them and puts himself in the open casement between her and the dark), Izek x2 (flat: "Not her." type of line; he is not afraid; the arm), Strahd x2 (courteous, a little amused; he steps back from the heat; "the brother"; no threat; he leaves), then Narrator x1 (the cold goes out of the room).

## Road lines for Izek as a guest (one line each, spoken aloud by Izek as he travels with the party; flat and short; under 24 words)

The nodes are named for when they play: place_vallaki (entering Vallaki: he does not look at the square), place_village (entering the village of Barovia: he nods at the churchyard), place_lake (entering the hill trail above Lake Zarovich or the lake itself: he does not say what it is), place_castle (entering Castle Ravenloft: the rider; quiet, cold), fight_arm (after a fight: the arm; he hid it), fight_ireena (after a fight: he looked at her first; "Is she hurt?" in his way), idle_doll (on a long walk: the doll in his coat), idle_wait (on a long walk: "I'm good at waiting" in a new form that is not those words), idle_dark (on a long walk: it is quiet and he listens to the trees).

## Epilogue lines (one slide of text each; our words; two sentences at most; under 40 words)

These are epilogue slides shown when the story ends, about what became of Izek. Write EIGHT, named like this: izek_a to izek_d for the ending where the vampire lord is destroyed and izek_e to izek_h for the ending where he is not.
- izek_a / izek_e: Izek walked with Ireena to the end and stayed her guard ("guarding").
- izek_b / izek_f: Izek was told the truth and left the Baron, and lives, alone, near the woods past the lake ("told").
- izek_c / izek_g: Izek was refused by the Baron when he asked for her as his reward, and waits ("spurned").
- izek_d / izek_h: Izek is dead, and Ireena never knew him ("dead").
For the ending where he is not destroyed, the mood is darker: nobody is safe; the guarding Izek is still there; the told Izek hears the castle's carriage on the road.

## The game and the format

This is dialogue for a single-player D&D Curse of Strahd game. Plain text only (no JSON, no markdown tables), nodes under `~ name`, one line per row as `Speaker [mood]: Text`, party option rows as `* option text -> node_name` (the player's character speaks, first person, short, under 14 words, no skill checks), ASCII only (straight quotes and apostrophes, no accents or fancy dashes, no em-dash: use a comma or a full stop), 1-2 sentences a line, nothing over about 28 words, no placeholders like {name}. Moods allowed: [smile], [angry], [afraid], [sad], [sly], [weary]; most lines carry none. Finish without sending messages to anyone else.

## Who they are

IZEK STRAZNI: a big, scarred man who was the Baron of Vallaki's enforcer. His right arm is not his own: scaled red-black to the shoulder, clawed, hot to the touch, able to burst into flame. When he was nine, wolves came out of the trees by the lake and took his little sister and his arm; he woke with this one. He has dreamed of a red-haired woman every night since and paid the toymaker Blinsky to carve her face into dolls, a chest of them at the foot of his bed. The party has now told him that the woman is Ireena Kolyana, his lost sister (found wandering on a road as a girl, no memory, raised by the burgomaster Kolyan of Barovia). He believed it. He walked out of the Baron's service ("I won't break any more heads for that fat fool in the sash. I'm done."). He talks to the dolls at night (his secret; he does not say so). How he talks: short, flat, imperatives and threats; never more than two sentences unless about her; about her he goes quiet and almost gentle, which is worse; calls the Baron "my lord" and later "that fat fool". Pet phrases: "Stand back from the Baron." "Not here." "I'm good at waiting." He never says Strahd's name: "him", "the rider", "the castle". He is not funny; the humour is around him. Moods: [angry], [sad] or none.
Some of his existing lines, so you hear him (do NOT repeat them): "You're in my room." / "Good. I've wanted to since the gate." / "She's real. I dream her every night. Her face, her hair." / "I've seen you. Every night since I was nine years old. I didn't know your name. Now I do." / "My sister. My sister had red hair." / "I won't touch her. I won't let anyone touch her." / "I remember enough for both of us." / "I'm good at waiting. A man with one room and a long memory doesn't have to hurry."

IREENA KOLYANA: a proud, red-haired young woman, the dead burgomaster Kolyan's adopted daughter, found on a road as a girl with no memory of where she came from, twice bitten by the vampire lord Strahd. Direct and proud; short sentences; dry humour with an edge; grim joke before anyone can pity her; never says Strahd's name ("him", "the devil", "our visitor"). She does not remember Izek; she said "I don't remember you. I wish I did." She does not fight in this game: something in the valley goes round her like water round a stone. Pet phrases (at most once per scene): "I'm not made of glass." "Say it plainly." "Father would want it done properly."
NARRATOR: old gothic storyteller, second person or plain scene description, present tense, one or two sentences, the second a turn; concrete senses; never cruel; no game terms.

## Canon limits for everything

No new named characters. Real names you may use: Izek, Ireena, Ismark (her brother by adoption, a big, earnest man), Kolyan (their father), Blinsky (the toymaker), Baron Vargas (the Baron), Lake Zarovich, Vallaki, Barovia, Krezk, the Blue Water Inn, St. Andral's church, Father Lucian, Urwin (the innkeeper), Emil (a werewolf who saw the night). Do not name Strahd. Do not invent other names, numbers, places or history; do not describe the sister's name or past except where a node says so. The "Viorela" name appears ONLY in the node that says so. No quest hints, no directions, no promises of rewards. No dice or skill checks.
result:
~ window_izek_inn
Narrator: Izek stands wide awake in the doorway of Ireena's room at the Blue Water Inn, his scaled arm glowing red like a forge coal. The heat of it smells of ash and hot iron.

~ window_izek_krezk
Narrator: At the top of the stairs behind Krezk's wall, the shutters hang open to the night. Izek stands wide awake in the doorway, his scaled arm lit red like a forge coal.

~ izek_window
Narrator: Izek walks past you without a word and plants himself in the open casement between Ireena and the dark. Fire licks up the black scales of his shoulder.
Izek: Not her. Go back to the castle.
Izek [angry]: You want through this window, you burn first.
Strahd [smile]: The brother. How very warm you keep her threshold.
Strahd: Step easy, my friend, for I have no quarrel with kin tonight. The dark will keep until the fire goes out.
Narrator: He steps back into the empty air and is gone between one breath and the next. The frost melts from the sill, and the cold goes out of the room.

~ place_vallaki
Izek: Keep walking past the square. That fat fool can hang his own lanterns.

~ place_village
Izek: That is the churchyard where Kolyan lies. He kept her safe when I could not.

~ place_lake
Izek: Keep to the trees above Lake Zarovich. I have no use for that water.

~ place_castle
Izek: The rider's house is cold. Stay behind my right shoulder.

~ fight_arm
Izek: Don't look at the arm. The fire goes down when the work is done.

~ fight_ireena
Izek: Leave my coat, it's only blood. Look to Ireena first and see if she is hurt.

~ idle_doll
Izek: Blinsky used good wood for the face. I keep one in my coat so the rain doesn't spoil it.

~ idle_wait
Izek: Nine years old to now is a long sit by a door. Another mile is nothing.

~ idle_dark
Izek: Too quiet in these pines. Something is listening back.

~ izek_a
Narrator: When the mist lifted from Barovia, Izek walked beside his sister into the sun and never asked her for a memory. He sits by her door still, a quiet dog with a warm right hand.

~ izek_b
Narrator: Izek left Vallaki behind and built a cabin near the woods past Lake Zarovich, where he lives alone. When Ireena passes the road below, he watches from the trees and lets her go in peace.

~ izek_c
Narrator: Spurned by Baron Vargas and denied the reward he asked for, Izek walked out of the town gates alone. Even with the valley free, he waits in a rented room with a chest of carved dolls.

~ izek_d
Narrator: Izek Strazni went into the earth with his monstrous arm and his secret unbroken. Ireena walked out of the valley into the sunlight and never knew she had another brother.

~ izek_e
Narrator: No roof in the valley is safe for long while the castle stands above the mist. Whenever the night grows cold, Izek sits awake across Ireena's threshold with his scaled arm burning like a coal.

~ izek_f
Narrator: Alone in a cabin near the woods past Lake Zarovich, Izek keeps his axe by the door and sleeps little. On windless nights he hears the castle's black carriage rolling down the road toward the villages.

~ izek_g
Narrator: Baron Vargas refused him the girl he had dreamed of since he was nine, and the night never ended. In a dark room in Vallaki, Izek sits over his chest of Blinsky dolls and waits.

~ izek_h
Narrator: Izek Strazni died in the fog with a chest of red-haired dolls left behind in his room. The devil still rules the valley, and Ireena never knew the brother who dreamed her face.
